rationale: Canonical evidence_span must declare what representation its digest actually hashes; one universal hash basis would counterfeit precision across byte-addressable files, exact text surfaces, and provider-extracted DOCX/File-Library content. Permit three explicit bases. (1) SOURCE_BYTES_RANGE when exact source bytes plus stable byte offsets are available; this is the strongest raw-source basis. (2) EXACT_UTF8_SPAN when the authoritative retrieval surface exposes exact text but not stable raw byte offsets; hash the exact retrieved span encoded as UTF-8 without semantic, whitespace, Unicode, or line-ending normalization, and bind the digest to source/version/locator plus retrieval representation. (3) VERIFIED_EXTRACTION_REPRESENTATION for non-byte-addressable rich/container sources only when a deterministic extraction representation can be reproduced; hash the exact extraction output and bind extractor identity/version, representation contract, source identity/version, and locator. This third digest is a digest of the verified extraction representation, never a raw-source digest. A summary, paraphrase, named-section label, OCR guess, or privacy projection cannot masquerade as any of these exact spans. Consumers that specifically require raw-byte proof may accept only SOURCE_BYTES_RANGE; other evidence requirements may accept the latter bases only within their declared extraction fidelity. Missing source bytes remain an explicit evidence ceiling, not something a representation hash repairs.
